requirements.title: Complete native geometry and asynchronous reset
requirements.description: The complete instruction_cache and supplied dependencies are in scope, with no top parameters. Fixed macros select 32-bit addresses, eight warps, two fetch mask bits, 32 sets, two ways, 64-bit lines, four MSHR entries and two subentries per entry. Address bits31:8 are tag,7:3 set and2:0 byte offset. Every native input pattern is legal. Active-low rst_n asynchronously clears all pipeline registers, both SRAM arrays and read/bypass registers, all validity and replacement state, MSHR address/target/valid/sent state and both response FIFO slots/pointers. Initial replacement way is zero. There is no core request or response ready port.

requirements.title: Two-stage core response and unconditional payload
requirements.description: On each rising edge stage1 captures current request address, warp and mask unconditionally, and valid captures core_req_valid_i with same-cycle matching flush removed. Stage2 captures prior stage1 address/warp/mask unconditionally; its valid is prior stage1 valid with current stage1 matching flush removed. Data captures the pre-edge 64-bit lookup data from the hit way, with way0 on no hit and way1 if both ways hit. Return the complete line without selecting by byte offset; mask is echoed without gating lookup or data. All payload outputs remain observable while valid is zero. Miss status is stage1 valid AND no tag hit, first suppressed by the previous stage0 flush and captured one edge, then suppressed by the registered stage1 flush; status is not an earlier-stage combinational result. Misses respond immediately with status1 and stale selected-way data; there is no internal core replay.

requirements.title: Warp flush and retained miss processing
requirements.description: A stage0 flush matches current core_req_wid_i and flush_pipe_wid_i when flush valid: it suppresses both array read enables and the captured request valid. Stage1 matching uses the stored request warp; it suppresses next core response valid and the corresponding registered status. A current stage1 flush does not suppress that stage1 miss entering MSHR. Flush affects neither cache storage/replacement nor existing MSHR entries, memory requests or refills. Other warps continue independently.

requirements.title: Tag validity, replacement and invalidate priority
requirements.description: Tag hit requires the captured read-request valid, a matching captured tag for the stored request address and the current validity bit of its captured set. In both-way hits the binary way is one. A miss selects way0 for data. Each set independently replaces way0 after reset and thereafter replaces the opposite of its most recently touched way. A lookup hit touches its hit way; a refill touches its pre-edge replacement way. A hit and refill in one set give the lookup touch priority; different sets both update. A refill sets only the selected way valid and has priority over global invalidation. When no refill occurs, invalid_i clears all way validity bits but preserves SRAM contents, replacement state, MSHR, FIFO and pipeline. An invalidation coinciding with a refill is discarded, with no pending invalidate.

requirements.title: Synchronous array reads and full-way collision bypass
requirements.description: A nonflushed core request captures both ways' pre-edge tag and data values for its current set. With no read, the array read registers retain their prior values. If the same edge also refills that set, the SRAM read is suppressed and a one-edge bypass flag instead selects two copies of the refill tag and two copies of its complete64-bit line, including the way not written. Otherwise the read registers are selected. This full-way bypass is intentional observable behavior and does not use the refill way mask. Bypass data/tag captures every edge from the currently selected response head and refill address; reset clears it. Underlying SRAM writes still modify only the pre-edge replacement way.

requirements.title: MSHR admission, merging and simultaneous response reuse
requirements.description: A stage1 miss offers block address addr[31:3] for one edge. Each of four entries is live when either of its two subentries is valid; a matching live address is secondary. Match encoders bitwise-OR all matching entry indices, returning0 on no match. Allocation uses the lowest free entry or subentry, returning0 when none exists. Reject a primary when all entries are live, a secondary when its two slots are full, or any miss concurrent with a response for the same block. Rejected misses are dropped without core backpressure/retry. An admitted primary writes its block address at the pre-edge lowest free entry. Normally it sets that entry's subentry0; concurrent response for a different block clears the matched response entry and places this new valid bit at the smaller of the free-entry and response-entry indices, while the block write remains at the original free entry. Thus reuse can revive the old response address. An admitted secondary sets its chosen slot, with new valid bits taking priority over concurrent clearing. Without an admitted request, a response clears all subentries of its selected entry.

requirements.title: Memory request scheduling and packed source truncation
requirements.description: For each entry keep a sent flag. The lowest-index live unsent entry drives mem_req_valid_o; with none eligible select index0 for observable address/source payload and deassert valid. Request address is that entry's29-bit block concatenated with three zeros. A valid/ready handshake sets its sent flag; a response clears the selected response entry's sent flag, with a same-entry request send taking priority. The target-information input truncates the nominal concatenation {warp,addr[2:0]} to only addr[2:0]. Keep a24-bit target vector reset to zero. An admitted request for entry e and subentry s writes three offset bits starting at bit3*((e+1)*(s+1)-1). mem_req_a_source_o reads bits3*send_entry+:3, including the resulting aliasing between entry0 secondary and entry1 primary, and entry1 secondary and entry3 primary. No warp bits survive this source path. Payload remains observable while memory request valid is zero.

requirements.title: Response FIFO, refill selection and native fallback
requirements.description: mem_rsp_ready_o is always one. A two-slot FIFO captures every valid memory response and consumes each nonempty head at the following rising edge; it has no empty bypass, may simultaneously enqueue/dequeue and preserves stale slot payload while empty. Its99-bit payload is {data64,address32,source3}; response source is otherwise ignored. The head address bits31:3 match all live MSHR blocks and bitwise-OR matching entry indices; no match selects entry0. Every consumed head refills the stored block address of that selected entry, not the raw external response address, using its current replacement way, stored block tag/set and the head's full64-bit data. Unsolicited or duplicate responses therefore use entry0's stale block and clear its MSHR validity. Response acceptance/consumption is independent of core valid, flush, invalid and memory request readiness. Complete native high bits and all documented concurrent reset/read/write/admission priorities remain in scope.
